subtopic: Calibration / MinMax vs Percentile vs KL
learningObjective: Compare MinMax, Percentile, and KL-divergence calibration for PTQ activation scales.
stem: For PTQ activation calibration to INT8, which of the following statements about MinMax, Percentile (e.g., 99.9%), and KL-divergence (entropy) calibration are TRUE? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: MinMax uses the observed absolute maximum activation across the calibration set as the clipping threshold; it is simplest but very sensitive to outliers that inflate the range and waste INT8 levels on rare extremes.
Percentile calibration (e.g., 99.9%) discards the top 0.1% of activations, keeping the range tighter and dedicating INT8 levels to the bulk of the distribution at the cost of clipping true outliers.

KL-divergence (entropy) calibration searches for a threshold that minimizes the KL divergence between the FP activation distribution and the quantized distribution; TensorRT's default INT8 calibrator uses a variant of this.
MinMax is always the most accurate calibration because it never clips any true activation value.
KL calibration requires that the scale grid is FP (continuous); it cannot be applied to INT8 quantization because the target grid is discrete.

explanation: A, B, C are standard characterizations of the three calibration modes. MinMax's outlier sensitivity is well-documented; percentile trades a bit of clipping for a tighter distribution fit; KL calibration is TensorRT's classical INT8 workflow. D is false: MinMax's no-clip property means outliers dominate the scale and starve the bulk distribution of resolution — 'not clipping' is not the same as 'most accurate'. E is false: KL calibration is defined against a discrete quantization grid; TensorRT's entropy calibrator explicitly operates on histograms mapped to INT8 bins.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: MinMax definition and outlier sensitivity.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: KL calibration definition; TensorRT's default.
optionExplanations.E: Wrong: KL calibration operates on discrete grids.

assumptions: Symmetric per-tensor quantization; scale determined by threshold.
The calibration set is representative of inference-time activations.
nonImplications: Does not imply KL is universally better than MinMax; for narrow distributions with no outliers, MinMax is fine.
Does not imply percentile is a fixed threshold; 99%, 99.9%, 99.99% are common tunable choices.
